gaps.sentence: The report must ___ before Friday's board meeting.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive: must be + submitted. 'Been' would require have (must have been submitted).

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ (inspect) twice a year for signs of corrosion.
gaps.explanation: 'Twice a year' marks a routine: present simple passive, is + inspected.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ (say) to be on the verge of bankruptcy.
gaps.explanation: It is said that... → The company is said to be... Present simple passive: is said.

gaps.sentence: The ancient scrolls are far too brittle ___ .
gaps.explanation: The scrolls receive the action: passive infinitive to be + unrolled.

gaps.sentence: Guests ___ to arrive no later than seven.
gaps.explanation: Guests receive the request: present simple passive are + asked.

gaps.sentence: My laptop ___ (service) next week, so back up your files beforehand.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' takes the future passive: will be + serviced (is being serviced is also a valid arrangement).

gaps.sentence: A cheaper version of the vaccine ___ right now.
gaps.explanation: 'Right now' requires present continuous passive: is being + developed.

gaps.sentence: All new students ___ (give) a locker key on their first day.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: are + given. Passives of give keep the indirect object as subject.
